Usage: ai-proxy [options] [command]

OpenAI-compatible local proxy for Grok, GitHub Copilot, and other AI providers

Options:
  -V, --version                    output the version number
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose logging
  --readme                         Print this tool's README and exit
  -h, --help                       display help for command

Commands:
  up                               Start ai-proxy (and optional public exposure
                                   tunnel)
  down                             Stop ai-proxy only (never stops shared
                                   cloudflared tunnel)
  install [options]                Install the launchd agent so ai-proxy starts
                                   at login and respawns on crash (macOS)
  uninstall [options]              Unload and remove the launchd agent (the
                                   proxy stops)
  status [options]                 Show ai-proxy and public exposure status
  serve [options]                  Start the OpenAI-compatible proxy server
  models [options]                 List proxy model ids and metadata
  sessions [options]               One row per session record: accounts, model,
                                   requests, tokens, cache hit %, losses, last
                                   error
  session [options] <id> [action]  One session: its record, then one row per
                                   request with cache read, write, hit % and
                                   losses. `use` switches its accounts (no
                                   restart)
  stats [options]                  Cache totals per agent: hit %, its spread per
                                   request and per session, losses by cause
  monitor [options]                Live requests and compaction events, one line
                                   each (filters: session, model, compaction,
                                   slow, errors)
  calls [options]                  Query proxied calls
                                   (session/stage/label/model/slow) and open
                                   full transcripts
  link [options]                   Register this proxy as an AI-config account
                                   so @proxy/<slug>/<model> refs resolve
  clients                          Manage per-user client keys + usage ledger
  introspect|ls [options]          Print full copy-paste inventory for Cursor
                                   BYOK
  config                           Manage ai-proxy config (interactive menu when
                                   run without subcommand)
  usage [options]                  Show subscription or Management API usage
  accounts                         Manage configured accounts
  internal                         Internal maintenance commands
  help [command]                   display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy up [options]

Start ai-proxy (and optional public exposure tunnel)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy down [options]

Stop ai-proxy only (never stops shared cloudflared tunnel)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy install [options]

Install the launchd agent so ai-proxy starts at login and respawns on crash
(macOS)

Options:
  --json      Machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy uninstall [options]

Unload and remove the launchd agent (the proxy stops)

Options:
  --json      Machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy status [options]

Show ai-proxy and public exposure status

Options:
  --json      Machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy serve [options]

Start the OpenAI-compatible proxy server

Options:
  --port <number>            Listen port
  --host <host>              Listen host
  --translate-cursor <mode>  Cursor translation mode: auto|on|off
  --thinking <mode>          Thinking presentation: raw|cursor|folded
  --no-translate             Disable Cursor translation
  -h, --help                 display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy models [options]

List proxy model ids and metadata

Options:
  --provider <slug>    Filter by provider slug
  --visibility <tier>  Filter by visibility: high|medium|low
  --json               Machine-readable output
  --cursor-ids         Print only proxy ids
  -h, --help           display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy sessions [options]

One row per session record: accounts, model, requests, tokens, cache hit %,
losses, last error

Options:
  --open          Only sessions that are still open
  --since <when>  Sessions active since a duration (1d, 7d) or a local date
                  (default: "7d")
  --json          Machine-readable output
  -h, --help      display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy session [options] <id> [action]

One session: its record, then one row per request with cache read, write, hit %
and losses. `use` switches its accounts (no restart)

Options:
  -f, --follow                Keep printing the session's new requests as they
                              come
  --json                      Machine-readable output
  --codex <account>           use: run the session's Codex turns on this login
                              or proxy account
  --claude <account>          use: run the session's Claude turns on this login
                              or proxy account
  --grok <account>            use: run the session's Grok turns on this login or
                              proxy account
  --allow-metered <account>   use: allow this per-token account (repeatable)
                              (default: [])
  --marker <id>               compaction-drop or compaction-restore: exact
                              blocked compaction ID
  --from <file>               compaction-restore: saved record file
  --acknowledge-context-loss  compaction-drop: explicitly accept loss of the
                              earlier context
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy stats [options]

Cache totals per agent: hit %, its spread per request and per session, losses by
cause

Options:
  --session <id>      One session only
  --agent <agent>     codex, claude (or anthropic), grok, other
  --since <when>      A duration (1d, 7d) or a local date (default: "7d")
  --from-transcripts  Read Claude Code's own transcripts instead of the proxy
                      ledger (the agent comes from the model id)
  --json              Machine-readable output
  -h, --help          display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy monitor [options]

Live requests and compaction events, one line each (filters: session, model,
compaction, slow, errors)

Options:
  --session <prefix>  Only this session: the proxy record, Claude Code's id, or
                      a request's session tag
  --model <text>      Only models whose id contains this
  --compaction        Only compaction requests and compaction events
  --slow <secs>       Only requests at least this slow (events always print)
  --errors            Only failed requests and warning events (retry, missed,
                      wasted, failed, blocked)
  --since <minutes>   Print the last N minutes first
  --once              Print the --since backlog and stop
  --json              One JSON object per line
  -h, --help          display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy calls [options]

Query proxied calls (session/stage/label/model/slow) and open full transcripts

Options:
  --session <id>        Filter by x-gt-session (substring)
  --stage <name>        Filter by x-gt-stage (exact)
  --label <text>        Filter by x-gt-label (substring)
  --model <text>        Filter by proxy model id (substring)
  --slower-than <secs>  Only calls at least this slow
  --since <minutes>     Only calls from the last N minutes
  --limit <n>           Max rows (newest kept) (default: "40")
  --show                Print the full prompt + response of each match
  --timeline            Show per-call phase breakdown (dispatch, TTFB, thinking,
                        text)
  --json                Machine-readable output
  -h, --help            display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy link [options]

Register this proxy as an AI-config account so @proxy/<slug>/<model> refs
resolve

Options:
  --status    Report the link without changing anything
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy clients [options] [command]

Manage per-user client keys + usage ledger

Options:
  -h, --help            display help for command

Commands:
  list                  List configured clients (keys masked)
  add [options] <name>  Add a client; prints its generated key ONCE
  secure                Move plaintext client keys into the vault (config keeps
                        only a reference)
  usage [options]       Per-client monthly usage (JSON, or CSV for invoicing)
  help [command]        display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy clients list [options]

List configured clients (keys masked)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy clients add [options] <name>

Add a client; prints its generated key ONCE

Options:
  --token-cap <n>       Monthly total-token cap
  --cost-cap <usd>      Monthly cost cap in USD
  --provider <type...>  Restrict to provider types (never subscription types)
  -h, --help            display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy clients secure [options]

Move plaintext client keys into the vault (config keeps only a reference)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy clients usage [options]

Per-client monthly usage (JSON, or CSV for invoicing)

Options:
  --month <YYYY-MM>  Month to report (default: current UTC month)
  --csv              CSV output
  -h, --help         display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy introspect|ls [options]

Print full copy-paste inventory for Cursor BYOK

Options:
  --json            Machine-readable output
  --show-secrets    Include full proxy API key in output
  --clipboard       Copy output to clipboard
  --section <name>  accounts|endpoints|models|cursor|all
  --account <name>  Limit to one account
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy introspect|ls [options]

Print full copy-paste inventory for Cursor BYOK

Options:
  --json            Machine-readable output
  --show-secrets    Include full proxy API key in output
  --clipboard       Copy output to clipboard
  --section <name>  accounts|endpoints|models|cursor|all
  --account <name>  Limit to one account
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy config [options] [command]

Manage ai-proxy config (interactive menu when run without subcommand)

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Commands:
  setup-tunnel    Interactive cloudflared tunnel setup for Cursor (public URL)
  detect          Detect local Grok, GitHub Copilot, and API keys
  init [options]  Initialize config from detected accounts
  show            Show current config (redacted)
  set [options]   Update config values

Usage: ai-proxy config setup-tunnel [options]

Interactive cloudflared tunnel setup for Cursor (public URL)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy config detect [options]

Detect local Grok, GitHub Copilot, and API keys

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy config init [options]

Initialize config from detected accounts

Options:
  --append    Add detected providers the config has no account for, leaving
              existing accounts untouched
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy config show [options]

Show current config (redacted)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy config set [options]

Update config values

Options:
  --port <number>                  Listen port
  --proxy-key <key>                Proxy API key
  --translate <mode>               Cursor translation mode
  --thinking <mode>                Thinking presentation: raw|cursor|folded
  --public-hostname <host>         Public hostname for Cursor, e.g.
                                   proxy.example.dev
  --public-base-path <path>        URL prefix on hostname, e.g. /ai
  --exposure-mode <mode>           none|cloudflared|tailscale|custom
  --public-base-url <url>          Custom Cursor base URL (…/v1) when
                                   mode=custom
  --tunnel-name <name>             cloudflared tunnel name
  --cloudflared-config <path>      Path to cloudflared config.yml
  --cloudflared-auto-start <bool>  Start tunnel on up (true|false)
  -h, --help                       display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy usage [options]

Show subscription or Management API usage

Options:
  --account <name>   Limit to one account
  --provider <type>  Filter by provider type or slug (e.g. openai-subscription,
                     codex)
  --json             Machine-readable output
  --recent <n>       Include last N local request records
  --breakdown        Per-model aggregates over the trailing 30 days
  --paths            Print local usage store file paths
  -h, --help         display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts [options] [command]

Manage configured accounts

Options:
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Commands:
  login <provider>              OAuth login for a provider (github-copilot,
                                codex)
  status                        Auth detail for codex accounts (source, expiry,
                                plan)
  bind [options] <name>         Point a codex account at a managed login (tools
                                codex login), instead of the Codex CLI's
                                auth.json
  set-routing [options] <name>  Pin an OpenRouter account's provider routing
                                (order/only/ignore/sort/fallbacks)
  list                          List configured accounts
  test <name>                   Ping upstream for an account
  disable <name>                Disable an account (kept in config, skipped at
                                runtime)
  enable <name>                 Re-enable a disabled account
  failover <name> [state]       Show or set (on|off) whether a Codex account
                                moves to its failover list by itself; off by
                                default, so the error reaches the client
  set-key <name> [key]          Choose an api-key account's credential (omit key
                                for a masked interactive chooser)
  allow-env [options] <name>    Non-interactive form of set-key's env choice
                                (clears any stored key; --off revokes)
  remove <name>                 Remove an account from config
  help [command]                display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts login [options] <provider>

OAuth login for a provider (github-copilot, codex)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts status [options]

Auth detail for codex accounts (source, expiry, plan)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts bind [options] <name>

Point a codex account at a managed login (tools codex login), instead of the
Codex CLI's auth.json

Options:
  --codex <login>  The managed openai-sub login, e.g. one listed by `tools
                   ai-proxy accounts status`
  -h, --help       display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts set-routing [options] <name>

Pin an OpenRouter account's provider routing (order/only/ignore/sort/fallbacks)

Options:
  --match <glob>            Scope to one per-model route instead of the
                            account-level default (exact id or a trailing *)
  --order <providers>       Comma-separated provider names, most preferred first
  --only <providers>        Comma-separated provider names — route ONLY to these
  --ignore <providers>      Comma-separated provider names to never route to
  --sort <mode>             price|throughput|latency
  --allow-fallbacks         Allow OpenRouter to fall back beyond the
                            pinned/allowed providers
  --no-allow-fallbacks      Refuse fallback — only the pinned/allowed providers
                            may serve the request
  --require-parameters      Only route to providers supporting every parameter
                            in the request
  --no-require-parameters   Allow providers that silently drop unsupported
                            parameters
  --data-collection <mode>  allow|deny
  --fallback-models <ids>   Comma-separated OpenRouter model ids to try if the
                            primary one fails
  --clear                   Remove all provider-routing pins for this account
  -h, --help                display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts list [options]

List configured accounts

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts test [options] <name>

Ping upstream for an account

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts disable [options] <name>

Disable an account (kept in config, skipped at runtime)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts enable [options] <name>

Re-enable a disabled account

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts failover [options] <name> [state]

Show or set (on|off) whether a Codex account moves to its failover list by
itself; off by default, so the error reaches the client

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts set-key [options] <name> [key]

Choose an api-key account's credential (omit key for a masked interactive
chooser)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts allow-env [options] <name>

Non-interactive form of set-key's env choice (clears any stored key; --off
revokes)

Options:
  --off         revoke the opt-in
  --env <NAME>  Read the key from this env var instead of the provider's default
                name
  -h, --help    display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy accounts remove [options] <name>

Remove an account from config

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy internal [options] [command]

Internal maintenance commands

Options:
  -h, --help               display help for command

Commands:
  update-models [options]  Probe upstream models and write
                           ~/.genesis-tools/ai-proxy/models-catalog.json
  help [command]           display help for command

Usage: ai-proxy internal update-models [options]

Probe upstream models and write ~/.genesis-tools/ai-proxy/models-catalog.json

Options:
  --account <name>   Limit to one account
  --provider <slug>  Filter by provider slug (grok, github-copilot)
  --dry-run          Print would-be catalog without writing
  --no-probe         Picker catalog only
  -h, --help         display help for command
